cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers at Colossae (Colossians 1:1-2), and he just told them to do whatever they do, in word or deed, in the name of the Lord Jesus (Colossians 3:17). Now he speaks to a household, one person at a time. First up, the wives: "Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord."

cards.question: Next, Paul turns to the husbands. He tells them to love their wives and not be harsh with them.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to the children and tells them to obey their parents in everything.

cards.question: Paul tells children to obey their parents in everything. What reason does he give?

answers.text: It is pleasing to the Lord
It brings them a long life
It keeps the home at peace

cards.question: Paul warns fathers that provoking their children can leave the children discouraged.

cards.text: Next, Paul speaks to slaves and tells them to obey their earthly masters in everything.

cards.question: Paul says slaves shouldn't obey only to please their masters at certain times. Which times?

answers.text: When the masters give a reward
When the masters are in a good mood

cards.question: Instead, Paul wants the slaves to obey with ___ of heart and fear of the Lord.

cards.text: Then Paul says whatever you do, work at it with your whole being. Your WHOLE being, friend, not just the half that hit snooze three times and is still negotiating with the pillow.

cards.question: Paul tells the slaves they will receive something from the Lord as their reward. What is it?
Paul tells the slaves that in the end they are really serving their earthly masters.
Paul says that when it comes to repaying wrong, some people get favoritism.

cards.text: Now Paul flips it around and talks to the masters, since they also have a Master in heaven. And friend, NOBODY in this house is off the hook.

cards.question: Paul tells the masters to supply their slaves with what is right and ___.

cards.text: Paul is still writing to the believers in Colossae, and now he moves from the household to prayer. He tells them to devote themselves to prayer and to stay watchful.

cards.question: Paul wants them devoted to prayer and watchful. What else does he want them to be as they pray?

cards.text: Then Paul asks them to pray for him and those with him too. And friend, he's writing this in chains.

cards.question: Paul is in chains, and he asks them to pray that God will open something for him and those with him. What?
Paul says he is in chains for the mystery of Christ.

cards.text: Paul also asks them to pray that he may declare the mystery of Christ clearly, as he should.

Then Paul turns to how the believers treat outsiders, and he tells them to be redeeming the time. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer counting falling dust, friend, so trust me, I'm a big fan of redeeming the time.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to stay away from outsiders.

cards.text: Act wisely toward outsiders, Paul says, and then he gets to how they talk: always gracious, seasoned with salt. Seasoned, friend, not SALTY, like the coworker who answers every email like it personally insulted him.

cards.question: Paul wants their speech always gracious and seasoned with salt. Why?

answers.text: So they know how to answer everyone
So they can win every argument
So people will speak well of them
